owner.why: the account the row belongs to, the value every RLS policy compares against

tenant.why: the organization the row is scoped to, null for a personal row

parent.why: the owning row, for a child object that has no owner of its own

project.why: the project the row is filed under, null when it is loose

createdBy.why: the principal that created the row, which is not always its owner

updatedBy.why: the principal that last wrote the row

version.why: the optimistic-concurrency token an If-Match precondition quotes

createdAt.why: when the row came into existence

updatedAt.why: when the row was last written

deletedAt.why: when the row was soft deleted, null while it is alive

originSurface.why: which product surface produced the row

facetSubjects.name: organization
facetSubjects.why: the billed tenant and the administrative boundary: the row every permission, policy and contract hangs off

facetSubjects.name: workspace
facetSubjects.why: the container content lives in. Exactly one primary workspace per organization, which is what every organization_id column already meant, plus one personal workspace per account

facetSubjects.name: membership
facetSubjects.why: one account bound to one organization, carrying the role, the status and the seat. There is no second membership table, so a workspace membership is this row

facets.subject: organization

facets.subject: organization

facets.subject: organization

facets.subject: organization

facets.subject: organization

facets.subject: organization

facets.subject: organization

facets.subject: organization
facets.claim: an organization allows and blocks connectors, plugins, MCP hosts and websites

facets.subject: organization
facets.claim: sharing outside the tenant is a permission the grid grants rather than a free action

facets.subject: organization
facets.claim: an organization publishes and retires the MCP servers its members may reach, versioned in the tenant

facets.subject: organization
facets.claim: the trust modes a tenant may permit are a contract, so local, BYOK and managed mean the same thing to every surface that offers them

facets.subject: organization
facets.claim: an organization names where its audit trail is delivered, which is what makes the scope of the trail the tenant and not the platform

facets.subject: organization

facets.subject: organization

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: a workspace has a stable surrogate id of its own, distinct from its organization id

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: a workspace belongs to one organization or to none, and a constraint makes the two scopes exclusive

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: a personal workspace is keyed to exactly one account, which is what gives it a stable id across sessions

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: a personal workspace is a row of its own with a kind, not the account: the account is public.profiles and the workspace is not

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: the workspace object every surface reads is one exported shape

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: the workspace list all six surfaces switch between is one exported shape, so a switcher shows the same rows everywhere

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: a workspace may pin the region it is processed in when a contract asks for one

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: a cost row names the workspace the usage was incurred in, which is the one dimension attributed to the container rather than to the funder

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: a workspace sets the model its members get by default

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: a workspace has no membership of its own: who may open it is decided by membership of its organization

source.instead: public.organization_members keyed by organization_id; a personal workspace has exactly one reachable account, its owner_account_id

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: content is not scoped to a workspace: every content table carries organization_id and none carries workspace_id

source.instead: organization_id on every content table, which resolves to the primary workspace one to one; provider_cost_events.workspace_id is the only column in the schema that names a workspace

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: policy layers are keyed to the organization, so a second workspace in one tenant could not be governed differently from the first

source.instead: organization_policy_overrides.organization_id with subject_type role, group, project, device or user

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: entitlement is a property of the tenant, not of the container

source.instead: organizations.billing_plan_tier, resolved for every workspace of that organization

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: the usage ledger is keyed to the organization, so what one workspace of a tenant spent cannot be read back from it

source.instead: organization_usage_ledger.organization_id for the funding dimension; provider_cost_events.workspace_id carries the container dimension and is not backfilled

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: retention is set per organization and per domain, never per workspace

source.instead: organization_domain_retention_policies keyed by organization_id and domain

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: no storage quota or bucket is scoped to a workspace

source.instead: organization_encryption_keys.key_region pins where a tenant key lives; file rows are scoped by organization_id

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: the defaults a container hands its members are stored against the organization, so two workspaces of one tenant share them

source.instead: organization_admin_policies keyed by organization_id

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: there are no workspace-wide instructions: the narrowest instruction scope is a project

source.instead: user_projects.instructions, which is per project and per account

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: a workspace cannot be disabled: nothing on the row says it is closed and no policy reads such a state

source.instead: suspending every membership of the organization one row at a time, or organizations.deletion_requested_at, which schedules removal rather than pausing use

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: a workspace cannot be archived; only content inside one can

source.instead: user_projects.is_archived and web_conversations.archived, which archive the content and not the container

facets.subject: workspace
facets.claim: a workspace cannot be moved between organizations, and the primary one cannot be removed while its organization exists

source.instead: organizations.data_region_requested moves a whole tenant between regions; there is no path that reparents a workspace

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: a membership names the account it binds

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: a membership names the organization it binds, and cascades with it, so no membership outlives its tenant

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: a membership carries a status, and only an active one confers permissions; deprovisioned is terminal

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: a membership carries exactly one built-in role

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: the Primary Owner is a generated fact of the membership row, so it cannot disagree with the role it is derived from

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: a membership carries the kind of seat it occupies

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: a membership records when the account joined

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: a member belongs to groups only through the directory: the join runs account to provisioned SCIM user to group, so a member who never came from the directory has none

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: an invitation is a row of its own with its own timestamps, so when somebody was asked is kept apart from when they joined

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: membership is the one ownership fact the settings surface resolves: it reads public.organization_members against public.organizations and no third table claims a seat

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: a membership has no surrogate id: it is identified by the pair of organization and account, so nothing can reference one membership by a single value

source.instead: the composite primary key (organization_id, user_id); every route addresses a member by the account id within the caller organization

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: there is no suspension timestamp: one column records the last transition whatever it was, so the time a member was suspended is lost the moment the row moves on

source.instead: organization_members.status_changed_at, overwritten by the transition trigger on every status change

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: there is no deprovision timestamp: the same status_changed_at carries it, and offboarding evidence therefore cannot distinguish a suspension from a removal after the fact

source.instead: organization_members.status_changed_at together with status = deprovisioned, which is terminal

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: a membership records no last activity, so an inactive seat cannot be found from the membership row

source.instead: device_installations.last_seen_at and account_sessions, which are per device and per session rather than per membership

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: no licence is assigned to a membership: seats are counted at the organization and the row carries only the kind of seat

source.instead: organizations.licensed_seats and seats_consumed for the count, organization_members.seat_type for the kind

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: a membership stores no entitlement snapshot or version, so what a member was entitled to at a past moment cannot be reconstructed

source.instead: organizations.billing_plan_tier resolved live at each request, with no per-membership record of what it was

facets.subject: membership
facets.claim: a membership stores no effective policy version: revisions are counted for the whole organization, so which revision governed one member is not recorded

source.instead: organization_policy_revisions.revision, which is per organization and per change rather than per member

duplicateVocabularies.why: both spell free/pro/max, one as what the account pays for and one as what a model requires. Every predicate in billing-catalog.ts already refuses to answer for the second, which is why scripts/check-plan-tier-predicates.mjs has to exempt six files.
the workspace policy list is the composer's Effort vocabulary retyped; a value added to one is silently unenforceable in the other.
the cross-surface chat contract carries its own spelling of the same six efforts.
the third copy of the effort vocabulary, and the pair that decides whether a policy can name what a client can send.
analytics names the product surfaces a second time, so a new surface reports under no name until both lists are edited.

columnExemptions.why: a Plaid item its owner linked; only the owner's own link, relink, account choice and removal write it, so there is no creator distinct from the owner, and no client edits it under an If-Match precondition

a hashed Ask from Siri credential its owner's app requests for one install; it is never edited, only revoked or replaced by the next rotation, so there is no creator distinct from the owner and nothing to version
the processor's dispute on a payment, written only by the Stripe webhook from the event; no principal other than the processor creates it and nothing edits it under an If-Match precondition
filed once by its owner and decided once by the platform, never edited by a client, so there is no creator distinct from the owner and no concurrent write to version

created, renamed and archived only by its owner in the developer console, so its creator is always its owner, and a rename or a new limit is a single last-write-wins edit that no If-Match precondition quotes

written only by the delivery job and the owner's resend, one row per attempt at an event, and never edited under an If-Match precondition, so there is no creator distinct from the owner and no concurrent write to version
registered, changed and removed only by its owner in the developer console, so its creator is always its owner, and each change is a single last-write-wins edit that no If-Match precondition quotes

recorded by the server for the account that reached the resource, so its creator is always its owner, and no client edits a reference under an If-Match precondition: a repeat sighting refreshes it in place

the value a published app saved under one key, written by the app through the runtime bridge and replaced whole: owner_user_id names the viewer it belongs to (null for the app's shared value), updated_by names the last writer, and no client edits it under an If-Match precondition

created only by its owner, when they confirm a link on the web or install the app into Slack, so its creator is always its owner, and it is never edited: a change is an unlink and a new link, which no If-Match precondition quotes

written by the server for the linked account when the app takes up a Slack message, so its creator is always its owner, and no client edits it under an If-Match precondition: its status moves only through the server's own transitions

one row per account, written only by that account's own enrollment, recovery and key changes, so its creator is always its owner, and each change is a single statement that no If-Match precondition quotes

a passkey or security key its owner registered; after that only a verified assertion moves its signature counter and only its owner removes it, so there is no creator distinct from the owner and no edit to version
one row per identity session that passed a passkey check, written by that check and swept once it expires; nothing edits it, so there is no creator distinct from the owner and nothing to version
a single-use WebAuthn challenge or browser handoff, created and consumed within minutes by the ceremony that minted it for its owner, so there is nothing to version
